cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-121971 - Symfony: ScopingHttpClient Sends the Credentials of Its Default Scope to Other Origins Through Network-Path References
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-121971
Published : Nov. 4, 2026, 6:17 p.m. | 53 minutes ago
Description :The component ScopingHttpClient in Symfony HttpClient merges the options of its default scope (such as auth_bearer or auth_basic) into a request before resolving a relative URL against the base_uri, allowing a network-path reference such as "//evil.example/steal" to be sent to another origin together with the default scope’s credentials, and resulting in potential disclosure of those credentials to an attacker-controlled server. This affects Symfony in versions 5.x prior to 5.4.56, 6.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11. The resolved URL falls outside the origin of the base URI, yet it keeps the merged options, whereas the absolute spelling "https://evil.example/steal" receives none. The same happens with a different port or user-info part on the same host. This is reachable whenever an attacker controls the beginning of a URL passed to a client built with a base_uri and credentials, including those created with HttpClient::createForBaseUri() or configured under framework.http_client.scoped_clients. To solve the issue, after resolving a relative URL against the base URI of the default scope, ScopingHttpClient now compares the scheme and authority of the result with those of the base URI, parsed the way the request is sent.
Severity: 8.2 | HIGH

The endpoint additionally requires an existing  ebootPath . The  /api/command  endpoint exposes debugger operations, including  write-memory ,  set-register , and  continue . The  /api/connect  endpoint can initiate outbound TCP connections. These operations can let an attacker execute an existing binary with the victim’s privileges, control the attached emulated process, or reach network services accessible from the host. CVE ID :CVE-2026-91168
Published : Nov. 4, 2026, 4:17 p.m. | 2 hours, 53 minutes ago
Description :Warpgate is an open source SSH, HTTPS, and MySQL bastion host for Linux. From 0.21.0 until 0.29.0, the Kubernetes request correlator in warpgate-protocol-kubernetes/src/correlator.rs keys an authorized AdmittedTarget by username, target_name, and client IP rather than by the immutable user UUID, while KubernetesSessionHandle::close does not evict the entry. If an account is deleted and a different low-privilege account is created with the same username, the replacement account can successfully authenticate as that recreated username and reuse the predecessor's still-live correlation entry when requesting the same target from the same client IP before kubernetes.session_max_age expires. Current-request authentication still occurs, but the reused entry bypasses a fresh target authorization check and can cause Warpgate to proxy requests with Kubernetes target credentials that the replacement account is not authorized to use, exposing cluster resources or permitting unauthorized mutations. This issue is fixed in version 0.29.0.

cvefeed.io Latest.description:

Published : Nov. 4, 2026, 4:17 p.m. | 2 hours, 53 minutes ago
Description :Warpgate is an open source SSH, HTTPS, and MySQL bastion host for Linux. Prior to 0.29.0, the Kubernetes protocol listener uses AcceptAnyClientCert in warpgate-protocol-kubernetes/src/server/client_certs.rs to accept certificates at the TLS layer and defer validation to warpgate-protocol-kubernetes/src/server/auth.rs, where authentication and lookup failures are rendered verbatim in an HTTP 500 response body. cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-121373 - Symfony: HtmlSanitizer MetaRefreshAttributeSanitizer Matches Only a Narrow Subset of the Browser Refresh Grammar (Incomplete Fix for CVE-2026-48761)
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-121373
Published : 4 de Novembro de 2026 às 13:17 | 19 minutos ago
Description :The Symfony HtmlSanitizer component MetaRefreshAttributeSanitizer, introduced to fix CVE-2026-48761, sanitizes the refresh URL of content attributes of meta tags using a regular expression that is too narrow, allowing sanitization to be bypassed, and resulting in potential URL redirection to untrusted sites in Symfony versions 6.1.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11. The shared declarative refresh steps in the WHATWG HTML Standard require a broader approach: the separator after the time may be ASCII whitespace alone, with no ; or ,, and the url= keyword is optional. Directives the browser honours, but the regular expression misses are returned unchanged, so the attacker URL skips UrlSanitizer entirely and both allowLinkSchemes and allowLinkHosts are defeated for the refresh navigation. This is reachable under any configuration that allows meta with http-equiv and content, including the documented allowStaticElements() preset.
Severity: 5.3 | MEDIUM

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-118516 - Symfony: Host Placeholders Can Match the Start of the Path in Compiled URL Matchers, Bypassing Path-Based Access Control
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-118516
Published : 4 de Novembro de 2026 às 13:17 | 19 minutos ago
Description :The Symfony Routing components CompiledUrlMatcher and UrlMatcher interpret the host and path information differently, allowing path-based authorization rules to be bypassed in Symfony versions prior to 5.4.56, 6.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11. For routes that define a host, CompiledUrlMatcher matches the string $host.'.'.$pathinfo against the host regular expression followed by the path regular expression, while UrlMatcher matches the host and the path separately. A host placeholder can therefore  match /, and consume the beginning of the path, so the request is routed to a controller, while UrlMatcher  would find no route. Rules that look at the path, such as access_control entries and firewall patterns, are evaluated against the actual request path, so they do not apply while the controller of the route runs, potentially allowing an unauthenticated request to reach a protected controller. For example, with the route /admin/report/{id}, the host app.{domain} and the rule access_control: [{ path: ^/admin, roles: ROLE_ADMIN }], an anonymous request for /admin/report/1 is sent to the login page. A request with the Host header app and path /x./admin/report/1 instead reaches the controller, with domain="/x". With the required domain: .+, the real hostname works: app.example.com and /x./admin/report/1 match with domain="example.com./x". Applications are affected if they have routes with host placeholders protected by path-based rules. With the default requirement, the Host header must be the host of the route without its last labels, such as app: framework.trusted_hosts blocks that, while a web server that only serves known names may not, for instance, Nginx passing the raw Host header to FastCGI for a request line that carries an absolute URI. If the requirement accepts /, such as .+, a real hostname works, and trusted_hosts does not help.
Severity: 6.3 | MEDIUM

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-118513 - Symfony: X.509 Authentication Impersonation via DN Value Injection (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-45063)
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-118513
Published : 4 de Novembro de 2026 às 13:17 | 19 minutos ago
Description :Authentication bypass by spoofing in X509Authenticator and X509AuthenticationListener of Symfony versions prior to 5.4.56, 6.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11 allows an attacker holding a certificate from the application's trusted CA who can influence the CN to authenticate as an arbitrary user of the application, including a privileged one, following an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-45063. X509Authenticator extracts the user identifier from the Subject DN (Distinguished Name) that the web server passes in $_SERVER['SSL_CLIENT_S_DN']. The fix for CVE-2026-45063 anchored that extraction to an RDN (Relative Distinguished Name) boundary, but the regular expression used was not escape-aware. The expression runs against an already serialized DN, so it cannot tell an RDN separator from a separator character that occurs inside a value. Under RFC 2253, used by Apache and by nginx's $ssl_client_s_dn, a comma inside a value is escaped as \, and the expression reads it as a separator regardless. RFC 2253 also does not treat / as a separator, so it leaves it bare inside a value, while the expression treats every / as one. The legacy X509_NAME_oneline() format, used by Apache's LegacyDNStringFormat and by nginx's $ssl_client_s_dn_legacy, is the mirror image: it escapes / as \/ and leaves , bare. In that format, a certificate with no emailAddress attribute, or whose poisoned CN precedes it, authenticates as the smuggled address. To cover both RFC 2253 and the legacy X509_NAME_oneline() format, X509Authenticator and X509AuthenticationListener now split the DN into RDNs before looking for the attribute, instead of matching the attribute against the serialized string. They select the separator from the serialization, split on unescaped occurrences of that separator only, unescape each RDN afterwards with the rules of its format, and require the attribute to span a whole RDN. The accepted value grammar is unchanged. Applications that pass a per-attribute user key (such as SSL_CLIENT_S_DN_Email) and deployments whose CA generates or validates the subject are not affected by this vulnerability.
Severity: 7.7 | HIGH

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-97693 - Yuxi sandbox isolation failure allows cross-tenant access and internal service compromise
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-97693
Published : Nov. 4, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 1 hour, 6 minutes ago
Description :Yuxi is a large-model-based intelligent knowledge base and knowledge graph agent development platform. From 0.6.0.beta1 until 0.7.1, there is insufficient isolation between execution-capable Docker sandboxes and trusted application services. A low-privileged authenticated user who can execute commands in their own sandbox can reach other tenants' sandbox APIs, access their files and secrets, execute commands in active sandboxes, and enumerate, create, or delete sandboxes through the unauthenticated provisioner without knowing administrator, database, or MinIO credentials. Sandboxes can also reach shared internal services; if shipped default service credentials remain unchanged, an attacker can use them, and if the exposed PostgreSQL account is a superuser, obtain command execution in the PostgreSQL container. These paths can disclose or modify cross-tenant data and sandbox state or cause denial of service through sandbox deletion without a container escape or kernel vulnerability. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.7.1. Existing deployments must separately rotate persisted PostgreSQL, Neo4j, or MinIO credentials that were previously set to documented or shipped defaults because upgrading the Compose files does not automatically rotate them.
Severity: 9.9 | CRITICAL

cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-57567
Published : Nov. 4, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 1 hour, 6 minutes ago
Description :Readest is a modern, feature-rich ebook reader designed for seamless cross-platform access and an intuitive reading experience. In affected desktop Tauri builds prior to 0.11.10, the apps/readest-app/src-tauri/src/transfer_file.rs commands download_file and upload_file accepted a webview-controlled file_path and passed it to File::create or File::open without checking the Tauri filesystem scope, rejecting absolute paths, or blocking parent-directory traversal. The commands were registered in the global invoke handler for the main, updater, and reader-* windows, so JavaScript executing in the privileged application origin could write attacker-controlled content to any path writable by the process or read and send any path readable by the process. Exploitation requires JavaScript execution in that privileged origin, such as through an application XSS or compromised renderer; whether book-embedded JavaScript can reach the parent origin was not established. The write primitive can overwrite trusted or startup files, while the read primitive can expose keys, tokens, and application secrets. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.10.
Severity: 8.6 | HIGH

Published : Nov. 4, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 1 hour, 6 minutes ago
Description :Readest is a modern, feature-rich ebook reader designed for seamless cross-platform access and an intuitive reading experience. Prior to 0.11.10, the unauthenticated /api/opds/proxy route in apps/readest-app/src/app/api/opds/proxy/route.ts accepted an attacker-controlled URL and fetched it server-side without restricting the scheme, blocking private, loopback, link-local, or metadata hosts, or revalidating destinations during automatic redirect following. Description :The component ScopingHttpClient in Symfony HttpClient merges the options of its default scope (such as auth_bearer or auth_basic) into a request before resolving a relative URL against the base_uri, allowing a network-path reference such as "//evil.example/steal" to be sent to another origin together with the default scope’s credentials, and resulting in potential disclosure of those credentials to an attacker-controlled server. This affects Symfony in versions 5.x prior to 5.4.56, 6.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11. The resolved URL falls outside the origin of the base URI, yet it keeps the merged options, whereas the absolute spelling "https://evil.example/steal" receives none. The same happens with a different port or user-info part on the same host. This is reachable whenever an attacker controls the beginning of a URL passed to a client built with a base_uri and credentials, including those created with HttpClient::createForBaseUri() or configured under framework.http_client.scoped_clients. To solve the issue, after resolving a relative URL against the base URI of the default scope, ScopingHttpClient now compares the scheme and authority of the result with those of the base URI, parsed the way the request is sent.

Description :SharpEmu is an experimental PlayStation 5 emulator for Windows and Linux. The frontend exposes an HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:8765 without authentication or CSRF token. Its  do_POST  handler in  tools/SharpEmu.DebuggerFrontend/debugger_frontend.py  does not validate the Origin, Referer, Sec-Fetch-Site, or Host headers. The  _read_json_body()  function also accepts JSON sent with browser-simple content types instead of requiring  application/json . A malicious page that can reach the loopback listener can send cross-origin requests to  /api/launch ,  /api/command , and  /api/connect . Chromium may require Local Network Access permission for pages served from public origins. Local-origin pages and other delivery paths are not consistently subject to this restriction. The  /api/launch  endpoint accepts an attacker-selected  emulatorPath  if it points to an existing file on the victim’s host. On POSIX systems, that file must also be executable. The endpoint additionally requires an existing  ebootPath . The  /api/command  endpoint exposes debugger operations, including  write-memory ,  set-register , and  continue . The  /api/connect  endpoint can initiate outbound TCP connections. These operations can let an attacker execute an existing binary with the victim’s privileges, control the attached emulated process, or reach network services accessible from the host. DNS rebinding can additionally let the attacker read API responses interactively. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.3-release.3-patch.1

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-115448 - Apache ZooKeeper: Unbounded recursion in snapshot serialization allows a client to render the server unrecoverable
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-115448
Published : Nov. 4, 2026, 11:17 a.m. | 2 hours, 35 minutes ago
Description :Uncontrolled recursion in Apache ZooKeeper. The server serializes its data tree to a snapshot by recursing one stack frame per znode level, with no depth bound. A client permitted to create znodes (the default root ACL is open) can build a chain of nested znodes deep enough that taking a snapshot exhausts the JVM stack and kills the snapshot thread; sizes stay within jute.maxbuffer, so existing limits do not prevent it. This is a denial of service that becomes persistent: on restart the server rebuilds the deep tree from its transaction log and fails again while taking the startup snapshot, so it does not return to service, and recovery can entail data loss. The same log affects a leader and its followers, so it can spread across an ensemble. This issue affects Apache ZooKeeper 3.8.0 through 3.8.7 and 3.9.0 through 3.9.6. Users are recommended to upgrade to 3.8.8 or 3.9.7, which fix the issue. As a workaround, use ACLs and authentication to restrict znode creation rather than relying on the default open root ACL.
Severity: 8.7 | HIGH

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-100252 - Apache ZooKeeper: SASL authorization bypass on the client port through a client-supplied authorization ID
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-100252
Published : Nov. 4, 2026, 11:17 a.m. | 2 hours, 35 minutes ago
Description :Improper Authorization vulnerability in Apache ZooKeeper. When SASL authentication is enabled on the client port, the server's SASL callback handler grants every authorization identity (authzid) that a client requests, without checking it against the principal the client authenticated as. The server then tries to replace the requested identity with a canonical form of the authenticated principal, derived from the zookeeper.security.auth_to_local rules. If no rule applies to the principal, canonicalization fails and the error is only logged. The client-requested authzid then becomes the session's SASL identity for all ACL checks. An authenticated client whose principal is not covered by the auth_to_local rules can therefore claim any SASL identity. With the default rules, this includes any Kerberos principal from a realm other than the server's default realm, such as a principal from a cross-realm trusted realm. The client then gets the permissions granted to that identity in sasl ACLs. If the requested identity matches a configured zookeeper.superUser, it gets superuser access to the whole data tree. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.8.8 or 3.9.7, which fixes the issue.
Severity: 8.6 | HIGH

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-87040 - Bluetooth LE Controller accepts received PDUs whose length field exceeds the configured maximum receive length, causing out-of-bounds read and write
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-87040
Published : Nov. 4, 2026, 6:17 a.m. | 7 hours, 35 minutes ago
Description :The nRF link-layer receive paths of the open-source Bluetooth LE Controller did not validate the on-air LENGTH field of a received PDU against the maximum receive length that was used to program the radio. isr_rx_pdu() in subsys/bluetooth/controller/ll_sw/nordic/lll/lll_conn.c enqueued any non-empty data PDU after only the sequence-number and (for encrypted links) MIC checks, and the corresponding isr_rx() handlers in lll_central_iso.c, lll_peripheral_iso.c, lll_sync_iso.c and lll_scan_aux.c did the same for ISO and extended-advertising PDUs. The nRF radio stores the received header verbatim and truncates only the payload at PCNF1.MAXLEN, so a frame declaring more octets than were configured leaves a node buffer whose len field describes more data than the buffer holds. An attacker within radio range that can emit a hand-crafted link-layer PDU — for a connection, any peer that establishes an unencrypted LE connection to a connectable advertiser; for CONFIG_BT_CTLR_SYNC_ISO, any broadcaster the device is synchronised to — can set the length byte up to 255 while the controller has programmed a much smaller maximum (lll->dle.eff.max_rx_octets, which is 27 until a Data Length Update, or the negotiated cis_lll->rx.max_pdu). No pairing, authentication or user interaction is required. On encrypted links the CCM MIC check normally rejects such a frame first, so the exposure is on unencrypted traffic, which is why the added check is placed after decryption. The unchecked length reaches hci_acl_encode() in subsys/bluetooth/controller/hci/hci.c, which performs net_buf_add(buf, pdu_data->len) followed by a memcpy() of that many bytes out of the node_rx pool element. Because CONFIG_BT_CTLR_DATA_LENGTH_MAX and CONFIG_BT_BUF_ACL_RX_SIZE both default to 27, this is an out-of-bounds read of up to roughly 228 bytes past the received PDU and a corresponding out-of-bounds write past the HCI ACL buffer into neighbouring buffers of the same pool; the tailroom test in net_buf_simple_add() is only enforced when CONFIG_NET_BUF_HARDENING (or CONFIG_ASSERT) is enabled. On the ISO paths the same unchecked length makes isoal_rx_append_to_sdu() read past the ISO node buffer and emit adjacent controller RAM to the host as ISO data. The practical result is remote memory corruption and controller crashes, plus disclosure of controller memory into the host data path. The fix rejects any received PDU whose length exceeds the value that was used to configure the radio reception. Note that lll_sync.c (periodic advertising sync reception) was not changed and still enqueues received PDUs without an equivalent bound.
Severity: 8.3 | HIGH
Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

CVE ID :CVE-2026-95860
Published : Nov. 3, 2026, 9:17 p.m. | 1 hour, 53 minutes ago
Description :node-opcua is an OPC UA implementation for TypeScript and Node.js. From 2.42.0 until 2.180.0, namespace-level access control configured through setDefaultRolePermissions is not honored by the runtime enforcement path for nodes without explicit per-node RolePermissions. SessionContext.getApplicableRolePermissions reads a missing or null DefaultRolePermissions metadata value instead of the configured namespace field, and the null result is treated permissively. An anonymous network client can consequently write variables with CurrentWrite access or call bound methods when an operator configured a restrictive namespace default and relied on inheritance. Servers with no declared policy, nodes with explicit per-node permissions, and correctly bound programmatic namespace metadata are outside the authorization-bypass case. This issue is fixed in version 2.180.0.

FortiGuard Outbreak Alerts.title: Atlassian Arbitrary File Access Vulnerability
FortiGuard Outbreak Alerts.description:
CVE-2026-21589 is a critical arbitrary file access vulnerability affecting multiple Atlassian Data Center products, including Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Software, Jira Service Management, Bamboo, Crowd, Crucible, and Fisheye. The vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to access specific files within an affected application's web root directory.
Exploitation requires the attacker to know the exact name and path of the target file in advance. The vulnerability does not provide directory listing or file enumeration capabilities by itself. Depending on the files exposed and the application configuration, successful exploitation could disclose sensitive information and potentially support further attacks.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: OT Refrigeration Control Systems Attack
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

November 2, 2026 Update: A new wave of suspected cyberattacks has affected supermarket refrigeration systems across several European countries, including Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland, and Estonia. Reported incidents involved attackers manipulating refrigeration controls and triggering defrost cycles or raising temperatures, with some equipment reportedly reaching 50°C. Affected retailers include ICA, Coop, Carrefour, Delhaize, Colruyt, and SuperValu. Sweden's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC-SE) confirmed it was responding to incidents involving ICA and Coop stores. However, authorities have not established whether these incidents are connected to the October attacks in France or share the same threat actors or infrastructure. No threat group has claimed responsibility, and no new malware or indicators of compromise have been publicly confirmed.

On October 11–12, 2026, attackers compromised refrigeration control systems at supermarkets across France, remotely manipulating refrigeration settings and triggering defrost cycles. The attacks caused temperatures in some refrigeration units to rise to as high as 50°C, resulting in food spoilage and operational disruption. Affected retailers reportedly included Intermarché, Netto, Carrefour, Coopérative U, Monoprix, and E.Leclerc.

France's national cybersecurity agency, CERT-FR, reported compromises involving Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers, as well as Copeland and Dixell XWEB systems. These systems monitor and manage commercial refrigeration and related building operations. Their compromise can allow unauthorized changes to operating parameters, potentially disrupting temperature control and damaging perishable goods.

Separate research by Claroty Team82 identified vulnerabilities affecting Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controllers, including:
CVE-2025-41450, an authentication bypass
CVE-2025-41451, an OS command injection vulnerability that can lead to remote code execution
CVE-2025-41452, a web server configuration vulnerability that can lead to denial of service
Danfoss released fixes for the above vulnerabilities, and organizations should update affected devices to the applicable patched firmware.

Additional research by Claroty Team82 and CISA documented vulnerabilities affecting Copeland XWEB Pro controllers, including:
CVE-2026-25085, an authentication bypass
CVE-2026-21718, an authentication bypass that can enable pre-authentication code execution
CVE-2026-24663, an unauthenticated OS command injection vulnerability
The affected Copeland models include XWEB300D PRO, XWEB500D PRO, and XWEB500B PRO running firmware version 1.12.1 or earlier. Organizations should consult the vendor's remediation guidance and apply the appropriate firmware updates.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

On October 12, France's national cybersecurity response team, CERT-FR, issued alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 warning of numerous compromises involving remote refrigeration controllers.

Organizations should immediately remove direct internet exposure from refrigeration controllers and restrict remote administration to secure VPN connections or protected management networks. Review controller configurations, particularly temperature settings and defrost schedules, and apply available firmware updates and vendor-recommended security settings. Change default credentials and replace unsupported, end-of-life devices where necessary.

If compromise is suspected, isolate affected equipment and follow vendor and CERT-FR recovery guidance before restoring operations. A factory reset alone is insufficient if the device remains vulnerable and exposed. Organizations should also segment OT networks from corporate IT environments, restrict access to authorized personnel, and monitor for unexpected changes to refrigeration settings.

Danfoss identifies firmware R4.2 as the fix for CVE-2025-41450 and R4.3.1 as the fix for CVE-2025-41451 and CVE-2025-41452. Verify the correct release against the specific device model.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Linux Kernel Remote Code Execution
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

FortiGuard Labs is monitoring CVE-2026-98432, a critical use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's IPv4 networking subsystem that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code with kernel-level privileges.

The vulnerability stems from improper memory management during TCP connection request processing. Under specific conditions, concurrent operations may access socket-option memory after it has been freed, resulting in a use-after-free condition.

An attacker can potentially trigger this flaw by sending specially crafted IPv4 TCP packets containing IP options to a vulnerable system. Exploitation requires precise timing but does not require authentication or user interaction.

Successful exploitation could result in kernel memory corruption, information disclosure, denial of service, or potentially remote code execution with kernel-level privileges.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

The vulnerability was introduced in Linux kernel 4.4. The upstream Linux kernel CVE team has published fixes for multiple supported kernel branches.

Ubuntu confirmed on November 2 that fixes for Ubuntu 22.04 and newer were available in its proposed repository while undergoing qualification testing. Ubuntu 26.10 already includes the fix.

Organizations running potentially affected Linux systems should:
1. Apply security updates: Install the latest kernel security updates provided by the respective Linux distribution.
2. Reboot affected systems: Restart systems after installing the updated kernel to ensure the patched kernel is running.
3. Restrict network exposure: Limit unnecessary inbound TCP connections from untrusted networks.
4. Filter IPv4 packets containing IP options: Red Hat provides an interim nftables rule to reduce exposure to the vulnerable code path.

• FortiGuard Labs continues to monitor CVE-2026-98432, including developments in exploitation research, vendor security updates, and the availability of security patches across affected Linux distributions.

• FortiGuard Labs will provide additional updates as new intelligence and protections become available.

The signature provides protection at the network layer, helping prevent exploitation attempts without requiring immediate changes to the underlying Linux kernel. FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Day Exploitation
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

FortiGuard Labs is monitoring active exploitation of multiple zero-day vulnerabilities affecting Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS), an enterprise remote access VPN solution. Threat actors have chained three vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2026-111357, and CVE-2026-118527) to achieve unauthenticated root-level code execution on vulnerable appliances.

According to security researchers, the attacks have been observed since at least October 1, 2026. The activity was initially attributed to a previously unidentified threat actor tracked by Volexity as UTA0576.

The attack chain begins with CVE-2026-104935, an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows remote attackers to execute commands without authentication. Attackers then leverage CVE-2026-111357 to escalate privileges and CVE-2026-118527 to upload attacker-controlled files to predetermined locations on the appliance.

Once access is obtained, observed post-exploitation activities include credential theft, Active Directory reconnaissance, data exfiltration, and network scanning. Researchers also reported attempts to retrieve Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) credentials and BitLocker recovery keys.

Notably, the attackers reportedly deployed no malware or web shells. Instead, they re-exploited the appliance to execute individual commands and manipulated system logs to conceal their activity and evade Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool.

Ivanti confirmed that exploitation affected a limited number of customers before disclosure. CISA has now added all three vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Ivanti Connect Secure appliances running the following versions are affected:
- Version 25.1.1.2 and earlier.
- Version 25.1.2.2 and earlier.
- Version 22.8R2.5 and earlier.

Organizations using Ivanti Connect Secure should immediately apply the latest available security updates.

Recommended actions:
- Upgrade Ivanti Connect Secure to a fixed release. Versions 25.1.1.3 and 22.8R2.6 address the two additional vulnerabilities. Organizations should follow Ivanti's current upgrade guidance for their specific release branch. Do not assume that installing the earlier October update for CVE-2026-104935 provides complete protection. The subsequent vulnerabilities require additional updates.
- Conduct network and memory forensics to identify potential signs of compromise. Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool alone may not identify all exploitation activity.
- If compromise is suspected, follow Ivanti's recovery procedures, including factory resetting affected appliances, rebuilding virtual instances where applicable, and upgrading to a fixed release.
- Reset potentially exposed administrator, domain, and local account passwords. Revoke and reissue stored certificates and reset API keys and other stored credentials.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

FortiGuard Labs continues to monitor exploitation attempts involving Ivanti Connect Secure and the associated attack techniques.

FortiGuard customers should use multiple layers of defense to help identify and mitigate suspicious activity associated with the exploitation chain:

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Node.js Brotli Remote Code Execution (Node2Shell)
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Google Brotli decoder, a component used to decompress data encoded with the Brotli compression algorithm. Brotli is widely used in web communications and is bundled with Node.js through its `zlib` module.

Brotli is an open-source project developed and maintained by Google for lossless data compression. It shrinks files so they can be transmitted faster without affecting the original data.

The vulnerability occurs when the decoder processes specially crafted Brotli-compressed input. An attacker who can supply malicious compressed data to a vulnerable application may corrupt adjacent memory, potentially leading to information disclosure, denial of service, or remote code execution.

The root cause is an error in the decoder's handling of malformed block-switch commands. Under certain conditions, the streaming decoder incorrectly treats an invalid block switch as a request for additional input rather than a format error. This can cause data to be written beyond the bounds of an internal eight-byte buffer, corrupting adjacent process memory.

The vulnerability affects Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0. Fixed versions include 1.0.10, 1.1.1, and 1.2.1, depending on the release branch. The Node.js project has also released patched versions for affected release lines.

On October 22, 2026, Imperva published research demonstrating remote code execution against a vulnerable Node.js build. Public proof-of-concept references are also listed in Red Hat's vulnerability bulletin, increasing the risk to unpatched deployments.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Organizations should prioritize updating vulnerable Node.js deployments and Brotli libraries to fixed versions. Because the vulnerability can lead to remote code execution, systems that process untrusted compressed content should receive particular attention.

Recommended actions:
1. Apply security updates: Upgrade Node.js to 22.23.4, 24.22.1, or 26.12.1, as appropriate, or a later fixed release. Update standalone Brotli packages to the applicable fixed version.
2. Review application exposure: Identify services that decompress untrusted Brotli data, including applications using node:zlib, HTTP clients processing compressed responses, and middleware that decompresses incoming request bodies.
3. Apply temporary restrictions where feasible: Until updates are deployed, limit untrusted Brotli-compressed traffic on affected application paths where operationally practical. Test any restrictions to avoid disrupting legitimate traffic.
4. Investigate suspicious activity: Review application and process logs for unexpected crashes or decompression errors. Correlate anomalies with incoming traffic and runtime versions; these symptoms alone do not confirm exploitation.
5. Rebuild and redeploy affected containers: Ensure production images and bundled dependencies include the patched runtime or library rather than relying solely on host-level updates.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

The vulnerabilities affect PHP, a widely used server-side scripting language that powers websites and web applications. They involve flaws in PHP's internal request-processing and memory-management behavior that can be triggered when handling malicious requests. Both are remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities rated as 9.2 (CVSS 4.0).

• CVE-2026-109618 - RCE via out-of-memory corruption: An out-of-memory condition can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Subsequent request-cleanup operations may incorrectly process this invalid data, potentially enabling remote code execution.

• CVE-2026-109619 - RCE via stale global state: Internal request state can persist after its associated memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may access this stale state before normal initialization resets it, potentially enabling remote code execution.

Successful exploitation could compromise the PHP application process and potentially provide access to sensitive server resources, application data, or databases, depending on the permissions of the affected process and the surrounding environment.

PHP announced emergency security updates for October 21, 2026, following reports that details of the vulnerabilities had leaked ahead of the planned disclosure. Subsequent reports highlighted ongoing exploit research and potential attack activity, underscoring the urgency of applying the available patches. However, widespread exploitation of either vulnerability has not been independently confirmed.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

The vulnerabilities affect PHP installations that process web requests, including deployments using PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed. PHP identifies Apache deployments using mod_php as particularly at risk because a demonstrated exploit can trigger before application code runs.

Organizations should prioritize patching internet-facing PHP servers and other exposed deployments immediately.
1. Apply the security updates. Upgrade to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35, as appropriate. Organizations using vendor-maintained packages should apply the corresponding security updates from their distributions or service providers.
2. Reduce exposure until patching is complete. Where immediate remediation is not possible, isolate affected systems from untrusted networks or temporarily disable exposed services when operationally feasible.
3. Review request-processing limits. Apply appropriate web-server or reverse-proxy limits for request sizes, input fields, multipart sections, headers, and nesting depth. These controls can reduce exposure but are not a substitute for patching.
4. Review potentially vulnerable systems. Investigate suspicious web requests, unexpected PHP worker behavior, unexplained process execution, and unusual access to application files or databases. Prioritize internet-facing systems and investigate potential compromise before returning affected services to production.

PHP 8.1 and older are no longer supported by the PHP project and do not receive its standard security updates. Organizations using these versions should check whether their operating-system vendor provides backported fixes or migrate to a supported release.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs recommends a defense-in-depth approach to reduce exposure to attacks targeting vulnerable PHP deployments and is currently monitoring the situation and will provide updates as new information becomes available and additional protections are released.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Citrix NetScaler RCE zero-day Vulnerabilities

Citrix confirmed that both vulnerabilities were exploited in the wild before security updates were available. CVE-2026-88772 is a memory overflow vulnerability that can lead to remote code execution or denial-of-service conditions. Fortinet PSIRT Advisories.title: Linux kernel RCE CVE-2026-98432
Fortinet PSIRT Advisories.description:
CVSSv3 Score: 9.8

CVE-2026-98432:ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it. Another cpu can concurrently process a retransmitted SYN for the same request socket, and send a SYNACK from tcp_check_req(). tcp_v4_send_synack() and inet_csk_route_req() read ireq->ireq_opt under rcu_read_lock() only, and ip_build_and_send_pkt() and ip_options_build() then read opt->optlen twice. Note that the SYNACK timer itself is not an issue: it holds a reference on its request socket, and inet_csk_reqsk_queue_drop() calls timer_delete_sync() before the child can be freed. Since commit 079096f103fa ("tcp/dccp: install syn_recv requests into ehash table"), request sockets are processed without holding the listener lock, so nothing prevents the child socket from being freed while the SYNACK is still being built. TCP child sockets do not have SOCK_RCU_FREE, and inet_sock_destruct() frees inet_opt with a plain kfree(), leading to a use-after-free in ip_options_build(). A similar issue exists with request socket migration (net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1, or a BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE program). reqsk_timer_handler() clones the request socket with inet_reqsk_clone(), so that the old request socket and its clone share the same ireq_opt, then reqsk_migrate_reset() clears the pointer in the old one. Another cpu holding a reference on the old request socket can still be using these options (sending a SYNACK, or creating a child in tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock()) when the clone is freed, and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() also uses a plain kfree(). Readers already use RCU, and other paths replacing inet_opt (do_ip_setsockopt(), cipso_v4_sock_setattr()...) already use kfree_rcu(). Use kfree_rcu() in inet_sock_destruct() and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() as well. IPv6 is not affected by the first issue, because tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock() duplicates the options. tcp_v6_reqsk_destructor() has the same migration issue with ipv6_opt, which is only set by CALIPSO. This will be addressed in a separate patch.
